title: Eyes to the Sky

source.title: Iranians brace for renewed attacks after Israeli, US elections
source.note: published 10-27 13:23 (page metadata, zone not stated); the 10-27 sweep (matched on 'iran'). Cut on 10-28 because no 10-28 sweep existed at run time (07:01 PT; GitHub's sweeps/index.json ends at 10-27) — the protocol's 'newest date' rule; the 10-27 queue's remaining rows were the day's queue. Newest unmarked AJ hit on a live object after yesterday's cut (the Moscow page 13:26 is six paragraphs and the 15:49 item is a video newsfeed — both filed in the pass, not cut). Non-US horizon, flagged. Read in full via the cloud fetch; reductions filed, no quotation over twelve words. A street page: the article, two anonymous Tehran residents, one X user; the force's two holders (Trump, Katz) as reported; Israel's opposition as reported

object.label: H6 — the Strait of Hormuz (PG01 layer 2), read from the force's side of the water and from Tehran's street: the naval blockade of Iran's southern ports (in place since July, Iran's oil exports halted — ¶14) as the instrument that keeps the water shut from Washington's end, and the strikes promised for after the two elections (¶3, ¶13, ¶15, ¶20) as the force's clock; the page's own subject is the street waiting for the jets. The Strait is not named on the page; the deal and the price are not on it

zAxis.pos: the force relents — the blockade lifts, no renewed strikes, the water reopens under the holder's 'U.S. control' and prices come down by it (the 10-11 words)
zAxis.neg: it does not — the blockade is prolonged by the holder's own threat, the strikes resume after the elections, and the water stays shut from both ends

transformNote: the shadow is the holder's 'U.S. control of the Strait of Hormuz' (10-11) as half the cure for prices 'COMING DOWN'. On this page the same holder's sentence is the opposite instrument: prolong the blockade of Iran's ports (¶14), strike the power plants and bridges if hostilities resume (¶13), 'death of a civilisation' (¶12). The control the shadow promised reopens the water; the control the page reports keeps it shut. Two sentences, one hand, sixteen days apart — reported as a series across sittings, not ruled

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: Iranians brace for renewed attacks after the elections; strikes teased, particularly against civilian infrastructure
lines.note: THE DOOR: the dek names the force's target class (civilian infrastructure) and its clock (the elections). 'Brace' is the page's verdict word
lines.zWhy: a street bracing for strikes after the vote is a water not reopening before it

lines.quote: Israelis have voted on Netanyahu; the US midterms on November 3
lines.note: the two clocks, dated — placement
lines.zWhy: two election dates read neither way on the water by themselves

lines.quote: since February 28: bombings, a blockade, sanctions
lines.note: the record's three instruments in one line; the blockade is H6's lock from Washington's end
lines.zWhy: a blockade listed among the war's instruments is a water shut from both ends

lines.quote: attacks fell sharply after the June memorandum; war fears have returned; many analysts expect strikes to resume after the elections
lines.note: the June MoU as the record (second Press sighting; aj 10-27 ¶9) and the clock set by 'many analysts' — attributed, undated
lines.zWhy: strikes expected after the elections are a force not relenting before them

lines.quote: more fighting whoever wins, Netanyahu or Eisenkot
lines.note: the street's first verdict: the Israeli clock does not change the force. Oscillation band
lines.zWhy: more fighting regardless of the winner is a water that stays shut regardless

lines.quote: Israeli rhetoric aims to overthrow the Islamic Republic, in power since 1979
lines.note: the force's purpose as the resident reads it — regime change (the `iran-strikes` terms); denominated toward the oscillation ceiling
lines.zWhy: a force aimed at the regime is a force with no price to relent for

lines.quote: opposition exists inside and outside Iran; cyber operations make online reactions hard to measure
lines.note: off the water — the page measuring its own instrument; vacancy
lines.zWhy: reactions hard to measure read neither way on the water

lines.quote: pro-Israeli Iranians called 'homeland sellers'; cooperation punished under national-security charges
lines.note: the state's denomination quoted; the water absent; vacancy
lines.zWhy: a charge for cooperation reads neither way on the water

lines.quote: January's protests, thousands believed killed; the UN: crimes against humanity by the security forces
lines.note: the record of the crackdown — right domain, a different plane from the water (surface-bound). Filed in the pass; no analog on the Press
lines.zWhy: a crackdown on the record is a force answered inward, not a water reopened

lines.quote: those who hoped for an overthrow are disillusioned; the blockade and sanctions have cut most incomes
lines.note: THE BLOCKADE AT THE COUNTER — the instrument's effect in Tehran, by a resident: the H1c mirror (the price from the other end of the water)
lines.zWhy: a blockade that cuts incomes is a water shut and paid for on this side too

lines.quote: views shifted after US and Israeli comments and strikes on infrastructure — oil and gas, power, steel
lines.note: the force's past targets named (oil and gas first); the resident reads the threats as already enacted once
lines.zWhy: strikes on oil and gas already made are a force that has not relented

lines.quote: most Iranians have no real choice and want stability and peace
lines.note: Rule 5 inside one voice: 26 → 30 → 34 across three lines — the resident's Dia rising as the water leaves the sentence
lines.zWhy: a wish for peace reads the force as the only variable

lines.quote: 'death of a civilisation'; the map might look different after the war
lines.note: constitutive — THE FORCE'S HOLDER, as reported and undated: the shadow's holder ('U.S. control', 10-11) in his other sentence. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: repeated threats to strike power plants, bridges, civilian infrastructure if hostilities resume; US media: the military ready to attack in the coming days if ordered
lines.note: THE READINESS: the force's clock at its shortest on the page ('the coming days if ordered') — the article attributes it to US media, not to the holder; `cand-post-election-strikes`, twelfth-plus sighting
lines.zWhy: a military ready in days is a force that has not relented

lines.quote: the other threat: prolong the naval blockade of Iran's southern ports, in place since July — oil exports halted, trade disrupted; with sanctions, poorer and more isolated
lines.note: THE INSTRUMENT, DATED, WITH ITS EFFECT: H6's lock from Washington's end — since July, Iran's oil exports at zero by it. The page's lowest-Dia line. The holder's 'control' of the water on the 10-11 page is this blockade on this one
lines.zWhy: a blockade prolonged by the holder's threat is a water the holder keeps shut

lines.quote: strike Iranian infrastructure again, energy facilities included; 'back into the Stone Age'
lines.note: constitutive — the other force's holder (Israel's defence minister), as reported. Not Dia-scored

lines.quote: Eisenkot, Bennett, Lapid and Golan praised the US-Israeli attacks, this war and last year's 12-day war
lines.note: the record of the opposition's position — the Israeli clock does not change the force (the resident's ¶4, confirmed by the article)
lines.zWhy: an opposition that praised the attacks is a vote that does not relent the force

lines.quote: the uranium stockpiles removed, the programme dismantled, the 'axis of resistance' eliminated
lines.note: the opposition's aims as the article frames them; the force's purpose stated from the other side
lines.zWhy: aims stated as removal and dismantling are a force with its purpose intact

lines.quote: government and opposition share the goal of overthrowing Iran's establishment; they differ on methods
lines.note: the article's verdict on the Israeli vote: one goal, two methods
lines.zWhy: one goal with two methods is a force whose clock the vote does not stop

lines.quote: military action cannot realistically topple the Islamic Republic; change must come from Iranians
lines.note: the challenge predicate: the force's own side doubting its purpose — a reader, stationed with the publication
lines.zWhy: a force doubted by its own side is still a force not yet relented

lines.quote: some Iranians are mentally preparing for conflict once the elections end
lines.note: the clock restated as the street's expectation
lines.zWhy: a street preparing for conflict after the vote is a water not reopening before it

lines.quote: groups formed with friends across the country to warn one another of strikes if they hear fighter jets overhead
lines.note: THE STREET'S DETECTOR: the page's one instrument built by the readers themselves — jets overhead as the primary
lines.zWhy: a warning network for jets is a force expected, sized by ear

lines.quote: domestic apps or texts, because the authorities may impose further internet and communication shutdowns
lines.note: the state's own clock on the force (a shutdown 'if needed') — the inward answer, dated to the same window
lines.zWhy: a shutdown prepared for is a force expected by the state too

lines.quote: ninety million people have their eyes to the sky for war
lines.note: THE TITLE: the page's most denominated line and its last — the force read as weather. Oscillation band, near its ceiling
lines.zWhy: eyes to the sky are a water nobody on the page expects to reopen
